test_title: PYST 14: SSC GD Constable 2024 - English (Held On: 23 Feb, 2024 Shift 2)
subject: english
question:
Choose the idiom/phrase that can substitute the highlighted group of words meaningfully.

I can't stand **a passenger in a car who gives unwanted advice to the driver, **like my mother-in-law.
solution:
The correct answer is: **Option 2.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The idiom **"Backseat driver"** refers to a passenger in a vehicle who gives unsolicited advice or directions to the driver. (अनचाही सलाह देने वाला)

 
 
• **Example:** My friend is such a **backseat driver,** always telling me how to drive.
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is: ***Backseat driver.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

 
• **Make No Bones About** (बिना किसी हिचकिचाहट के): To speak plainly and directly about something.

 
 
• **Example:** He made no bones about his dissatisfaction with the service.
 
 
 
• **Tongue And Cheek** (मजाकिया ढंग से): To say something in a humorous or ironic way.
 
 
• **Example:** His comments were meant to be tongue and cheek, but they were taken seriously.
 
 
 
• **Up in arms** (क्रोधित): To be very angry or upset about something.
 
 
• **Example:** The community was up in arms about the proposed construction project.
 
 

 

3a:Tb67,

The correct answer is: **Option 4.**
